A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FmCF/FmSS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, appendices A.1–A.7, and checklists support reliable comparison, including matching relocated displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original fairness-classification experiments, latent-dimension analyses, learned-representation visualizations, and an MNIST generation example in Section 6 and Appendix A.5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds an empirical study of CFD penalty-estimator variability across batch sizes in Appendix A.5, Table 4.

M1.justification: The FmCF characteristic-function penalty and FmSS moment-based penalty retain the same computations and objectives. Algorithm 1 changes the label 'decoder' to 'predictor', without changing its procedure; Algorithm 2 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adult, German, Crime, Compas, Health, and the MNIST example. The new batch-size study uses four existing datasets without adding task or population coverage. Law School remains explicitly unevaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–3 retain the same baselines and membership, as do the FNF Pareto comparisons. The added Table 4 evaluates only the FmCF estimator and introduces no comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 4 introduces a batch-size sweep of 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512 for estimator variability on Adult, German, Compas, and Health. Existing benchmark metrics, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a sensitivity analysis testing whether larger batches produce more reliable CFD estimates. The existing latent-dimension analyses in Figures 5–8 and MNIST case study in Figure 9 are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports standard deviations of the FmCF penalty estimator by batch size. The existing ten-seed averaging and 95% confidence intervals for the main Pareto comparison remain unchanged; no increase in repeated-run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds 28 estimator-standard-deviation values, including Adult values decreasing from 0.1150 at batch size 8 to 0.0007 at 512. Previously reported benchmark scores in Tables 1–3, plotted results, and MNIST outputs are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 5.1–5.3, their proofs, and the mathematical material in Appendices A.2–A.4 remain unchanged. Equation 2 merely renames the adversary notation. The added O(1/n) scaling remark interprets the batch-size results without adding a derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims about non-adversarial specialized representations, fairness guarantees, competitive accuracy, and deployment without sensitive attributes. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion explicitly adds that the moment-based approach is tailored to classification and needs extension for regression. Appendix A.5 also interprets decreasing estimator variability as improved reliability with larger batches, invoking expected O(1/n) variance scaling.

D1.justification: Table 4 supplies the exact batch-size grid for reproducing the new sensitivity study, although its estimator-specific resampling procedure is not explained. Existing preprocessing, implementation, hardware, optimizer settings, and code/data availability statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds brief historical framing connecting characteristic functions to longstanding statistical-testing literature and more recent machine-learning use, citing existing references [33] and [1]. The related-work section, bibliography, and positioning against competing fairness methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction with practical examples of specialized versus general representations, makes light wording and terminology edits, and adds acknowledgements and the conference header. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4, relocates the algorithm boxes, swaps the ordering and numbering of the Pareto and latent-distribution figures, and repositions the MNIST display. Existing figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new batch-size analysis provides useful, limited evidence about estimator reliability, while the application examples and explicit regression limitation improve clarity about scope. The central methods, proofs, and benchmark evidence remain unchanged. Sparse procedural detail for the new analysis limits the gain, but the additions support a modest overall improvement.
